research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9675 at 11 FR 333 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed January 5, 1946; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the January 8, 1946 issue. Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 15862 to 16749 of the held text, from the enacting words to the last operative sentence; the dossier span includes unrelated Federal Register page text. The order's heading and recitals precede it in the held text and contain no command. Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the St. Louis-San Francisco Railway Company and the St. Louis, San Francisco and Texas Railway Company, carriers, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the St. Louis-San Francisco Railway Company and the St. Louis, San Francisco and Texas Railway Company or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 9675 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
